Hit by this on v1.14.39 (macOS, TUI). Different root cause from the child-session dilution in #16270 and the directory-scoping issue @CasualDeveloper found in #13877.

Root cause: The path column was added to the session table at some point, but existing rows were never backfilled. Old sessions have path = NULL, sessions created after ~v1.14.29 have path = ''. The list query matches on path and NULL != '' in SQL, so pre-v1.14.29 sessions are invisible.
-- my database:
SELECT CASE WHEN path IS NULL THEN 'NULL' ELSE 'empty string' END, COUNT(*), MIN(version), MAX(version)
FROM session GROUP BY (path IS NULL);
-- NULL         | 520 | 1.4.9  | 1.14.19
-- empty string |  85 | 1.14.29 | 1.14.39

Workaround (fixed it immediately for me):
cp ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.bak
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "UPDATE session SET path = '' WHERE path IS NULL;"

Proper fix would be a migration that backfills path = '' where NULL on upgrade.
Unofficial extension to use for now: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=islee23520.opencode-sidebar-tui

I think this is the issue—disabled one MCP with many tools, and the issue is resolved.

This breaks the previous behavior and causes `opencode -c` in a parent to open the most recently closed child session (which may have been in a subdir) in the parent's pwd. This can lead the user to inadvertently effectively bypass their `external_directory` security setting as the session meant to be in the child path is now open in the parent, and now has access to all other children of that parent.

Your disable option kills the filtering entirely, which is even worse for users tripping over the above, and it leaves no way to restore the previous behavior. The prior behavior should have started as the default moving forward from this PR else all users will run into the above issue.

for anyone else running into this while the PR situation gets sorted out, I was able to create a port proxy in the windows firewall to forward the desired port on the windows machine down to the WSL network:
```ps1
# get the WSL IP
bash.exe -c "ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep -oP '(?<=inet\s)\d+(\.\d+){3}'"

# create proxy to forward windows port to WSL (admin required)
netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=<port> listenaddress=0.0.0.0 connectport=<port> connectaddress=<wsl_ip_from above command>
```
Once the forwarding rule is in place, I'm able to start opencode serve normally and reach it from anywhere on the LAN at `http://<windows_ip>:<port>`

Hope this helps anyone else who lands here!

Quick follow-up: I have done additional code analysis and identified the exact locations that need changes.

The root cause is in the message content schema validation. The internal schema uses `discriminatedUnion("type", [TextContentSchema, ImageContentSchema, AudioContentSchema])` where `ImageContentSchema` expects `type: "image"` with `data` + `mimeType` fields. However, the OpenAI-compatible provider converter correctly converts image file parts to `{ type: "image_url", image_url: { url: "..." } }` format, which then fails validation.

The fix would involve adding an `ImageUrlContentSchema` variant to the relevant discriminatedUnion, or alternatively converting the `image_url` format back to MCP-compatible `image` format before validation.

Happy to provide more details or test a fix if someone picks this up.

## Potential Duplicate Found

**PR #18752: "fix: preserve explicit model selection in command subtasks"**
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18752

This appears to be addressing the exact same issue as the current PR #26117. Both PRs aim to preserve command-selected models for command-triggered subtasks and prevent them from losing their model selection when spawning child subagent sessions.

**Why they're related:**
- Same core problem: command-triggered subtasks losing their explicit model selection
- Same solution domain: preserving model routing for command-triggered subtasks vs ordinary subtasks
- Both involve task tool spawning behavior and model precedence/fallback logic

While reviewing upstream history after opening this, I found that #18752 is already open and overlaps heavily with this PR. Both changes preserve command/subtask model selection through the delegation path and touch the same routing/test files.

The reason I’m leaving this open for now is that this version tries to keep the fix narrowly scoped to command-triggered subtasks and preserve existing behavior for ordinary/manual subtasks:
- only forwards the internal delegated model for command-triggered subtasks
- keeps ordinary/manual task-tool fallback behavior unchanged
- avoids pre-seeding child session agent/model so switch/history behavior stays aligned with existing prompt-time resolution
- includes regression coverage for fallback behavior and non-authoritative session metadata

If maintainers would prefer to converge on #18752 instead of reviewing two overlapping fixes, I’m happy to close this and upstream any useful guardrails/tests there.

I noticed this PR while researching subagent model-routing behavior and ended up opening #26117 before I found it. The two overlap heavily.

One difference in #26117 is that it keeps the internal delegated model scoped to command-triggered subtasks only, so ordinary/manual subtasks keep the existing fallback path. It also explicitly avoids pre-seeding child session agent/model after I hit a switch-event/history regression during QA, and adds regression coverage around fallback behavior and non-authoritative session metadata.

If it’s useful, I’m happy to help fold those guardrails/tests into this PR instead of splitting reviewer attention across two overlapping fixes.
